# Introduction

The primary purpose of the UKFE R package is to implement the regional
flood frequency methods outlined by the Flood Estimation Handbook (FEH;
available at
<https://www.ceh.ac.uk/data/software-models/flood-estimation-handbook>)
and associated updates. However, there are numerous other functions of
use to the hydrologist.

The UKFE package was initially developed by Anthony Hammond in 2020, and
he has been updating it regularly since then with additional
functionality and in response to new published methods and changes to
best practice.

In 2025, the Environment Agency commissioned JBA Consulting to undertake
testing of the package, to write this documentation and training
material and to assess future needs. Changes to the package for v1.0.0
were a result of this testing and funded by the Environment Agency. The
package has been updated since to account for changes to the FEH method
and for general improvements and bug fixes. The GitHub webpages
including vignette guides, function reference, and a change log, can be
found here: <https://agqhammond.github.io/UKFE/>. At the time of
writing, the training material is out of date.

# Contents

The ‘Changelog’ tab summarises updates in each version of the UKFE.

Under ‘Articles’, there are quick guides to the following topics:

- Basic R concepts and resources (R quick start guide).

- Data inputs.

- Data visualisation.

- FEH statistical analysis.

- ReFH analysis.

- Troubleshooting common errors.

There is also a ‘References’ article (under the “Articles” drop down,
not the references tab), which contains the references of books, user
guides or papers cited throughout the documentation.

There is no assumption that readers of these guides are experienced ‘R’
users, but there is an assumption of familiarity with the application of
the FEH methods. More detailed step-by-step guidance can be found in the
training material. There is an introduction to some R concepts that may
be useful in the ‘R quick start guide’ article.

Note that some of the information in the vignettes is based on that of
the FloodHydroStats website
(<https://www.floodhydrostats.com/ukfe-package-feh-quick-guide>).

# Hints and tips

For more information about the functions discussed in the guides and
further functions of the package, all the functions are detailed in the
‘References’ tab (with links to their help files) and in a PDF under
Reference Manual via the following link:
<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=UKFE>

Details can also be viewed in the package documentation within the ‘R’
environment. To get help with individual functions, you can type
`help(FunctionName)` or `?FunctionName`. If using RStudio, you can click
on the ‘Packages’ tab in the bottom right pane (assuming the default
layout), search for UKFE, and then click on it. You will then see a list
of functions; each can be clicked for more details. To get a list of the
function names, type `ls("package:UKFE")`.

Note that for any functions that take file paths, on Windows operating
systems, the backslashes will need to be changed to forward slashes, or
the file path will need to be stated as follows: `r"{my\file\path}"`.

Many of the examples throughout this documentation have the outputs from
running the code displayed below the code.

# Installation guide

It is recommended that the UKFE R package be used in RStudio (an
integrated development environment for R). You will first need to
install R from <https://cran.r-project.org/> and then RStudio can be
downloaded from
<https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/#rstudio-ide-oss-downloads>.

Once RStudio is open, the package must be installed and then loaded to
access its functions.

Note that installing the package only needs to be done once (although it
will need redoing if the UKFE package is updated or if you update your
version of R). Once you have installed the package, it will be saved in
your package library.

The package must be loaded from the library at the start of each new R
session to make its functions available.

The following commands can be entered into the console to carry out
these steps.

## Install from CRAN

Install the UKFE package: `install.packages("UKFE")`

## Install from GitHub

First, install the `remotes` package if you do not already have it
installed: `install.packages("remotes")`

Then, install UKFE directly from GitHub:
`remotes::install_github("agqhammond/UKFE")`

You may be prompted to update package dependencies — choosing option “1:
All” is recommended.

## Load the package

Once installed, load it into your R session:
[`library(UKFE)`](https://agqhammond.github.io/UKFE/)

You can also check the installed version with: `packageVersion("UKFE")`

# Data

Acknowledgement: Data from the UK National River Flow Archive.

This package is based on data from the National River Flow Archive
(NRFA). There is a pre-processing script that converts new releases of
the NRFA Peak Flow Dataset into data frames suitable for use within
UKFE.

Note that the unit tests include a small subset of data from the NRFA
Peak Flow Dataset, consisting of XML and AM files. This data sample can
only be used for test purposes. Please see the NRFA website
(<https://nrfa.ceh.ac.uk/>) for station metadata, the download of the
full peak flows dataset
(<https://nrfa.ceh.ac.uk/data/peak-flow-dataset>), and the data licence
(<https://eidc.ceh.ac.uk/licences/nrfa-data-terms-and-conditions-for-api-access-to-time-series-data-and-metadata/>).

# Feedback

If you have any feedback or suggestions, then please contact Anthony
Hammond at <floodhydrostats@gmail.com> or contribute to the GitHub
discussion page (<https://github.com/agqhammond/UKFE/issues>). You can
submit edits and additions to the package through GitHub.

# Package index

## Stats functions

Functions for carrying out statistical distribution fitting.

- [`GenLogAM()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenLogAM.md)
  : Generalised logistic distribution - estimates directly from sample
- [`GenLogEst()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenLogEst.md)
  : Generalised logistic distribution estimates from parameters
- [`GenLogGF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenLogGF.md)
  : Generalised logistic distribution growth factors
- [`GenLogPars()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenLogPars.md)
  : Generalised logistic distribution parameter estimates
- [`GenParetoEst()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenParetoEst.md)
  : Generalised Pareto distribution estimates from parameters
- [`GenParetoGF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenParetoGF.md)
  : Generalised Pareto distribution growth factors
- [`GenParetoPars()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenParetoPars.md)
  : Generalised Pareto distribution parameter estimates
- [`GenParetoPOT()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GenParetoPOT.md)
  : Generalised Pareto distribution - estimates directly from sample
- [`GEVAM()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GEVAM.md) :
  Generalised extreme value distribution - estimates directly from
  sample
- [`GEVEst()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GEVEst.md) :
  Generalised extreme value distribution estimates from parameters
- [`GEVGF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GEVGF.md) :
  Generalised extreme value distribution growth factors
- [`GEVPars()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GEVPars.md)
  : Generalised extreme value distribution parameter estimates
- [`GumbelAM()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GumbelAM.md)
  : Gumbel distribution - estimates directly from sample
- [`GumbelEst()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GumbelEst.md)
  : Gumbel distribution estimates from parameters
- [`GumbelGF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GumbelGF.md)
  : Gumbel distribution growth factors
- [`GumbelPars()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GumbelPars.md)
  : Gumbel distribution parameter estimates
- [`Kappa3AM()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Kappa3AM.md)
  : Kappa3 distribution - estimates directly from sample
- [`Kappa3Est()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Kappa3Est.md)
  : Kappa3 distribution estimates from parameters
- [`Kappa3GF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Kappa3GF.md)
  : Kappa3 distribution growth factors
- [`Kappa3Pars()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Kappa3Pars.md)
  : Kappa3 distribution parameter estimates
- [`Lcv()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Lcv.md) :
  Linear coefficient of variation (Lcv)
- [`LcvUrb()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/LcvUrb.md) :
  Urban adjustment for the linear coefficient of variation (Lcv)
- [`LKurt()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/LKurt.md) :
  Linear Kurtosis (LKurt)
- [`LMoments()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/LMoments.md)
  : Lmoments & Lmoment ratios
- [`LSkew()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/LSkew.md) :
  Linear Skewness (LSkew)
- [`OptimPars()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/OptimPars.md)
  : Optimise distribution parameters
- [`HistoricMLE()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/HistoricMLE.md)
  : Historic flood maximum likelihood estimation

## QMED functions

Functions relating to estimation of QMED (the median annual maximum
flow).

- [`QMED()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/QMED.md) :
  QMED (median annual maximum flow) estimate from catchment descriptors
- [`QMEDDonEq()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/QMEDDonEq.md)
  : QMED donor adjustment
- [`QMEDfseSS()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/QMEDfseSS.md)
  : QMED factorial standard error for gauged sites
- [`QMEDLink()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/QMEDLink.md)
  : QMED Linking equation
- [`QMED_FEH08()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/QMED_FEH08.md)
  : QMED (median annual maximum flow) estimate from catchment
  descriptors using the FEH 2008 method.
- [`DonAdj()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DonAdj.md) :
  Donor adjustment candidates

## Pooling group functions

Functions relating to the creation and use of pooling groups.

- [`Pool()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Pool.md) :
  Create pooling group
- [`PoolEst()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/PoolEst.md)
  : Pooled flood estimates
- [`PoolEst_FEH08()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/PoolEst_FEH08.md)
  : Pooled flood estimates using the FEH2008 method
- [`Pool_FEH08()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Pool_FEH08.md)
  : Create pooling group using the FEH08 method
- [`AddGauge()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/AddGauge.md)
  : Add an AMAX sample
- [`WeightsLCV()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/WeightsLCV.md)
  : Linear coefficient of variation (Lcv) weightings for a pooling group
- [`WeightsLSKEW()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/WeightsLSKEW.md)
  : Linear Skewness (LSKEW) weightings for a pooling group
- [`LRatioChange()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/LRatioChange.md)
  : Adjust L-Ratios in a pooling group
- [`WeightedMoments()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/WeightedMoments.md)
  : Weighted Lmoment ratios (LCV and LSKEW) from a pooling group
- [`Uncertainty()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Uncertainty.md)
  : Uncertainty quantification for gauged and ungauged pooled estimates
- [`QuickResults()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/QuickResults.md)
  : Quick pooled results

## Get data functions

Functions for retrieving, importing or viewing data.

- [`GetAM()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetAM.md) :
  Get an annual maximum sample from the National River Flow Archive
  sites suitable for pooling
- [`GetCDs()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetCDs.md) :
  Get catchment descriptors from the National River Flow Archive sites
  considered suitable for median annual maximum flow estimation (QMED)
  and pooling.
- [`GetDataEA_QH()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetDataEA_QH.md)
  : Get flow or level data from the Environment Agency's Hydrology Data
  Explorer
- [`GetDataEA_Rain()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetDataEA_Rain.md)
  : Get Environment Agency rainfall data (England).
- [`GetDataMetOffice()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetDataMetOffice.md)
  : Get regional Met Office average temperature or rainfall series
  (monthly, seasonal, and annual).
- [`GetDataNRFA()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetDataNRFA.md)
  : Get National River Flow Archive data using gauge ID.
- [`GetDataSEPA()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetDataSEPA.md)
  : Get Scottish Environment Protection Agency (SEPA) Flow, Level, or
  Rainfall data.
- [`GetQMED()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GetQMED.md)
  : QMED from a gauged site suitable for QMED
- [`AMImport()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/AMImport.md)
  : Import an annual maximum (AMAX) sample from NRFA peak flow .am files
- [`CDsXML()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/CDsXML.md) :
  Import catchment descriptors from .xml files
- [`CDsXML_Legacy()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/CDsXML_Legacy.md)
  : Import catchment descriptors from older .xml files

## Datasets

Datasets saved within the package.

- [`AMPF`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/AMPF.md) :
  National River Flow Archive (NRFA) annual maximum peak flow data for
  sites suitable for QMED only, and those for pooling.
- [`PeakFlowData`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/PeakFlowData.md)
  : National River Flow Archive descriptors and calculated statistics
  for sites suitable for QMED & pooling
- [`ThamesPQ`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/ThamesPQ.md)
  : Kingston upon Thames daily flow and catchment precipitation
  2000-10-01 to 2015-09-30
- [`UKOutline`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/UKOutline.md)
  : UK outline

## Diagnostic functions

Functions for obtaining diagnostics.

- [`GoFCompare()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GoFCompare.md)
  : Goodness of fit comparison (single sample)
- [`GoFComparePool()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/GoFComparePool.md)
  : Goodness of fit comparison (for a pooling group)
- [`H2()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/H2.md) :
  Heterogeneity measure (H2) for pooling groups.
- [`Zdists()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Zdists.md) :
  Zdist Goodness of fit measure for pooling groups
- [`DiagPlots()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DiagPlots.md)
  : Diagnostic plots for pooling groups
- [`AMplot()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/AMplot.md) :
  Plot of the annual maximum sample
- [`ERPlot()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/ERPlot.md) :
  Extreme rank plot
- [`EVPlot()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/EVPlot.md) :
  Extreme value plot (frequency and growth curves)
- [`EVPlotAdd()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/EVPlotAdd.md)
  : Add lines and/or points to an extreme value plot
- [`EVPool()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/EVPool.md) :
  Extreme value plot for pooling groups
- [`Seasonality()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Seasonality.md)
  : Seasonality plot

## Rainfall functions

Functions relating to depth duration frequency data.

- [`DDF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DDF.md) : DDF
  results from a DDFImport object
- [`DDF99()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DDF99.md) :
  FEH99 depth duration frequency precipitation model
- [`DDF99Pars()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DDF99Pars.md)
  : DDF99 parameters from .xml files
- [`DDFExtract()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DDFExtract.md)
  : Derive and plot rainfall Depth Duration Frequency curves.
- [`DDFImport()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DDFImport.md)
  : DDF13 or DDF22 results from .xml files

## Other time series functions

Functions for working with time series data (e.g. aggregating and
detrending data).

- [`AggMonDayHour()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/AggMonDayHour.md)
  : Aggregate a time series
- [`AnnualStat()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/AnnualStat.md)
  : Annual statistics extraction
- [`DeTrend()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DeTrend.md)
  : Linearly detrend a sample
- [`MonthlyStats()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/MonthlyStats.md)
  : Monthly Statistics
- [`POTextract()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/POTextract.md)
  : Peaks over threshold (POT) data extraction
- [`POTt()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/POTt.md) :
  Peaks over threshold (POT) data extraction (quick)
- [`TrendTest()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/TrendTest.md)
  : Trend hypothesis test

## Other hydrological functions

Functions that are not directly used for FEH analysis but may be useful
for other hydrological analysis.

- [`ARF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/ARF.md) : Areal
  reduction factor (ARF)
- [`BFI()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/BFI.md) :
  Baseflow index (BFI)
- [`DesHydro()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/DesHydro.md)
  : Design hydrograph extraction
- [`FlowDurationCurve()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/FlowDurationCurve.md)
  : Flow duration curve
- [`FlowSplit()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/FlowSplit.md)
  : Flow splitter
- [`HydroPlot()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/HydroPlot.md)
  : Hydrological plot of concurrent discharge and precipitation
- [`Rating()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Rating.md) :
  Stage-Discharge equation optimisation
- [`ReFH()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/ReFH.md) :
  Revitalised Flood Hydrograph Model (ReFH)
- [`SCF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/SCF.md) :
  Seasonal correction factor (SCF)
- [`UAF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/UAF.md) : Urban
  adjustment factor (UAF)
- [`UEF()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/UEF.md) : Urban
  expansion factor
- [`LowFlows()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/LowFlows.md)
  : Low Flows

## Other

- [`Bootstrap()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/Bootstrap.md)
  : Bootstrap
- [`ConvertGridRef()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/ConvertGridRef.md)
  : Convert between British National Grid Reference (BNG) and Latitude
  and Longitude or Irish Grid references.
- [`EncProb()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/EncProb.md)
  : Encounter probabilities
- [`NGRDist()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/NGRDist.md)
  : British national grid reference (NGR) distances
- [`NonFloodAdj()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/NonFloodAdj.md)
  : Non-flood adjustment
- [`NonFloodAdjPool()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/NonFloodAdjPool.md)
  : Non-flood adjustment for pooling groups
- [`SimData()`](https://github.com/agqhammond/ukfe/reference/SimData.md)
  : Data simulator
